<details style="margin: 0; padding: 0;">
<summary style="line-height: 1.2; margin: 0; padding: 2px 0;">
<span style="font-size: 1.2em;">Scalable numerical methods</span> (2026-Nov-24)
</summary>
<br>
<p>
This session discusses several fundamental mathematical problems that underpin many high-performance computing
(HPC) workflows and the numerical methods that may be used used to solve them at scale. We begin by
identifying where matrix-vector products, dense and sparse linear systems, and eigenvalue problems may appear
and consume the overwhelming majority of computational effort in various applications. We consider several
distinguishing problem characteristics and introduce corresponding numerical methods for their solution, as
well as a range of software libraries that implement these.
</p>
<ul>
	<li>Speaker: Sarah Huber (UVic)</li>
	<li><a href="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WestGrid/trainingMaterials/gh-pages/materials/20261124_Webinar_NumericalMethods.pdf" target="_blank">PDF slides</a></li>
</ul>
The recording will be spoted shortly.
